lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lying is hard work. You invent the story, remember it, and watch the other person.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Reverse order adds even more load. Truth-tellers just remember. Liars run out of room.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In a 2008 study, observers caught more lies when people told their story backwards.

lines.speaker: detective
lines.text: What about the eyes? Liars look to the left.

lines.speaker: reader
lines.text: A myth. Researchers tested it in 2012. Eye direction tells you nothing.

lines.speaker: reader
lines.text: Want the truth? Make the story work harder.
